# MockCRUD

**Instant mock APIs, generated by AI.**

MockCRUD is a web app for creating live REST APIs without writing a backend. Name a resource, add fields yourself or let AI infer them, or describe an entire system in one prompt and get a complete set of connected endpoints you can call right away.

🌐 **Live app:** [mockcrud.xyz](https://mockcrud.xyz)
⚙️ **Backend repo:** [AhmedKhawar/mockCRUD-backend](https://github.com/AhmedKhawar/mockCRUD-backend)

## What You Can Do

### 1. Add custom resources

Build your API resource by resource:

- **Name a resource** (for example `students`). AI checks that the name is valid before it is created.
- **Define fields manually.** Set a field name and type, and mark it as required or optional.
- **Infer fields with AI.** Tick **Infer fields**, choose how many fields you want, and AI generates them for you, including joins with your other resources.
- **Mix both.** A single submission can contain several resources, some manual and some inferred. A live summary shows how many resources you are creating and how many are manual or inferred.
- **Toggle Auth** per resource to protect it.

### 2. Generate a full system via prompt

Describe what you want to build, such as *"a hospital management system"*. AI designs the whole thing: every entity, its fields and types, and the relationships between them. It then creates all the resources and their live endpoints in one go.

### 3. Use and share your endpoints

Every resource you create shows up in your project with:

- Its five live endpoints: **GET all, GET by id, POST, PUT, DELETE**
- A ready-to-copy base URL
- Its fields and their types, shown next to each endpoint
- Options to collapse or delete the resource

MongoDB's `_id` is returned as `id` on each document, and that `id` is what you use for get by id, update and delete.

---

## How It Works

```
Create a project
      │
      ▼
Add custom resources  ──or──  Generate full system via prompt
      │                                  │
      └──────────────┬───────────────────┘
                     ▼
     Backend validates, generates schemas (AI) and registers endpoints
                     │
                     ▼
     Live REST API:  https://<api-host>/m/<projectId>/<resource>
```

This repository is the **frontend**. It talks to the [MockCRUD backend](https://github.com/AhmedKhawar/mockCRUD-backend), which handles AI generation, storage and serving the mock endpoints.

### Example endpoints

For a project with a `students` resource:

| Method   | Endpoint                          | Description        |
| -------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| `GET`    | `/m/<projectId>/students`         | Get all students   |
| `GET`    | `/m/<projectId>/students/:id`     | Get one student    |
| `POST`   | `/m/<projectId>/students`         | Create a student   |
| `PUT`    | `/m/<projectId>/students/:id`     | Update a student   |
| `DELETE` | `/m/<projectId>/students/:id`     | Delete a student   |

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- A recent Node.js LTS (20.19+ or 22.12+)
- A running instance of the [MockCRUD backend](https://github.com/AhmedKhawar/mockCRUD-backend), or use the hosted one
- A Google OAuth client ID (for sign-in)

### Installation

```bash
git clone https://github.com/AhmedKhawar/mockCRUD.git
cd mockCRUD
npm install
```

### Environment variables

Create a `.env` file in the project root. The names below are examples, so match them to the ones your code reads:

```env
VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:5000
VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=your_google_client_id
```

### Run locally

```bash
npm run dev
```

Then open the URL Vite prints, usually `http://localhost:5173`.

| `npm run preview` | Preview the production build       |
| `npm run lint`    | Lint the code with Oxlint          |

## Deployment

The app is set up for [Vercel](https://vercel.com) through `vercel.json`. Connect the repository, add the environment variables in your Vercel project settings, and deploy.
